question: What Does a 'Security Check Failed' Error at Checkout Mean?
metaDescription: It's a WordPress nonce (a short-lived security token) that expired — usually from the checkout page being left open too long before submitting.
shortAnswer: This message comes from a failed WordPress "nonce" check — a short-lived security token embedded in the checkout form specifically to prevent cross-site request forgery. Nonces expire after a set period (commonly around 24 hours, but effectively much shorter in practice for a form left open), so a customer who leaves a checkout tab open for a long time before submitting, or returns to it from a cached browser session, can trigger this even though nothing is actually wrong with their order.

bodyHtml:
Why This Happens

Nonces are WordPress's standard defense against cross-site request forgery, embedded as a hidden field in forms like checkout and verified on submission to confirm the request genuinely originated from that specific page load, not from a malicious external source replaying an old request. They're time-limited by design, which is the correct security behavior, but it does mean a checkout page left open too long, or loaded from a cached/bookmarked state, can fail this check on submission.

Common Causes

  • A customer leaving the checkout tab open for an extended period (browsing elsewhere, stepping away) before finally submitting, well past the nonce's effective validity window.
  • A caching plugin serving a stale, previously generated checkout page with an already-expired nonce baked into the cached HTML — checkout should always be excluded from page caching, and this is one of the clearest symptoms when it isn't.
  • Browser back-button navigation returning to a cached version of the checkout page rather than a fresh load.
  • Session or cookie issues (a browser blocking third-party cookies, or a session ending unexpectedly) breaking the nonce verification even on a relatively fresh page load.

How to Fix It

  1. Confirm checkout is properly excluded from any page caching — this is the most common underlying, fixable cause when the error happens frequently rather than occasionally.
  2. Ask affected customers to refresh the checkout page and try again if this happens as an isolated incident, since a fresh page load resolves it immediately.
  3. Check for cookie/session issues if the error persists even after a refresh, which points to a deeper session-handling problem worth investigating separately.
